::: {#exm-reals-uncountable}
#### The diagonal number for a list

Suppose a list of real numbers starts

$$
\ba
r_1 &= 0.\mathbf{7}071\ldots \\
r_2 &= 3.1\mathbf{4}15\ldots \\
r_3 &= -2.71\mathbf{8}2\ldots \\
r_4 &= 0.555\mathbf{5}\ldots
\ea
$$

The bold digits are the $n$th decimal places of the $r_n$: $7$, $4$, $8$ and $5$.
The proof of @thm-reals-uncountable builds $d = 0.5554\ldots$,
which differs from $r_1$ in the first decimal place, from $r_2$ in the second,
from $r_3$ in the third, and from $r_4$ in the fourth.
However the list continues, $d$ is not on it.

:::
